title: ReleaseHarnessAssertionKinds
description: What each assertion kind may promise, and exactly which fields the executor reads. This is the single definition shared by the draft schema, the contract schema and the execution adapter -- so a field the schema accepts is a field something consumes, and a field the executor honours is a field an author can discover. C1 exposed both halves of the gap: `expect: {}` reached 'ready to accept', and `expect.command` was accepted by the schema, taught by the project's own example, and read by nothing.

http.description: Exercise an HTTP endpoint. WHERE it lives is an execution binding; this says only what must be true of the response.

path.description: Path appended to the bound location. Defaults to /.

body_contains.description: Substring that must appear in the response body. D39: the real transfer test found the highest-value proposition available -- that the deployed service is running the revision intended for this release -- unwritable, because the service exposes it in the body and this kind could only read a status code. A substring test is the smallest primitive that closes it; anything richer is a query language, which this is deliberately not.

cli.description: Exercise a command. WHAT is executed comes from the execution binding -- an assertion never carries a command, because a command is a local fact about where things are installed, not part of a promise.

args.description: Extra arguments appended to the bound command.

stdout_contains.description: Substring that must appear in stdout.

stderr_contains.description: Substring that must appear in stderr. D40: well-behaved CLIs put diagnostics on stderr, so "the validator refuses for the expected reason" degraded to an exit-code check that any unrelated crash could satisfy. Note the distinction this preserves: stderr may be ASSERTED by an author who chose the expectation, but it is still never READ to attribute a cause -- the thing removed from the trust boundary was the harness guessing from stderr, not an author promising about it.

oneOfByKind.description: Non-standard annotation, read by the vocabulary-alignment test rather than by a validator: maps each executable kind to the definition above that describes its expect payload.
